text.p: Slovenian trading company Kovinotehna said on Wednesday its 1996 preliminary pre-tax profit rose to about 300 million tolars ($1.94 million) from 18.8 million a year earlier.
"The main reasons for the rise were improved organisation, lower costs and an increase in trading with the former Yugoslav republics," deputy chief executive Milena Sedovnik said.
She said the company's 1996 sales were about 34 billion tolars, almost unchanged from the previous year. Investment of 700 million tolars was also on a par with 1995.
"Most of our investment went into the construction of new shops. In the future we do not plan any major investment except for reconstructing existing facilities," Sedovnik added.
She said the company would decide about its dividend at a shareholders' meeting, expected at the end of June or beginning of July.
Kovinotehna shares were five tolars down at 446 tolars in late morning trade.
